VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: The claim applies to every closed subset of ℝ, including the empty set. For nonempty closed C, the distance function d(x,C) yields a zero set and the G_δ representation; the empty set is handled separately by the constant function 1 (zero set) and by openness (G_δ). The target’s concrete proof for C = {0} is correct, and the general case is fully covered by the cited theorem thm-metric-spaces-are-tychonoff-and-perfectly-normal. The remark about “the same two formulas” exhibiting any closed set is imprecise for the empty case, but the special case is trivial and introduces no counterexample.
